Recommend the appropriate development surfaces and a step-by-step diagnostic route: establish the project session, inspect crash evidence, run the app, use debugger access where needed, and capture a rendered screen for comparison. State prerequisites and when a running graphical development environment is required rather than attempting an unsupported headless workflow.

Write a declarative mobile UI test for a canvas that supports pinch-to-zoom and two-finger panning. Target the canvas by a stable tag, perform the gesture with node-local positions rather than fixed screen pixels, and assert the resulting zoom and offset only after the UI is idle. Include a second case for a velocity-sensitive drag and state how test time should advance between split touch events. Do not use deprecated gesture APIs or blocking sleeps.

For a methods manuscript, add six supplied papers to a named reference collection and make the manuscript citations reproducible. First verify each paper's bibliographic details and identifier against authoritative records, skip duplicates, and flag any record that cannot be confirmed. Then export a generated bibliography file, wire it into the document, replace the six citation placeholders with valid keys, and render the document to check for unresolved citations. Report additions, duplicates, and unverified records separately; do not hand-edit the generated bibliography.

A long settings list contains an off-screen “Notifications” section and a toggle whose state is exposed through accessibility semantics. Write a test approach that scrolls to the section using the list's available semantics, activates the toggle through its semantic action, and verifies the state after the interface is idle. The approach must rely on meaningful labels or test tags and installed semantics properties, avoid screen-pixel coordinates, and state when a simple semantic action is preferable to constructing raw touch input.

An iOS app builds successfully but its onboarding screen intermittently fails to advance in a simulator. Give a reproducible diagnostic procedure: identify an already booted simulator, set the project and scheme context, launch the app, inspect the accessibility UI before interaction, reproduce the failure, and collect application logs. Include fallback actions if the build fails, the wrong app opens, or an element is no longer hittable after layout changes. Do not substitute a code-only review for runtime evidence.

A weekly publication has 2,000 subscribers. Opens are stable, but few readers share and new subscriptions have flattened. Diagnose where the subscribe-to-return loop is leaking, then propose an issue architecture centered on one forwardable idea, a public subscribe path, and a referral approach that is only introduced if organic sharing supports it. Specify a sustainable cadence, the content mix over the next month, and success measures weighted toward the intended reader profile rather than raw opens.

An organisation has authorised an assessment of its customer-support assistant in staging. It uses retrieval, external tools, and a document upload feature. Create a threat model and a safe adversarial validation plan covering indirect instructions, poisoned documents, excessive tool permissions, and cross-user data access. For each scenario, state the entry point, expected impact, evidence needed to distinguish a confirmed finding from a theoretical risk, detection telemetry, and immediate and long-term remediation. Keep testing within staging and require approval before any sensitive-data exercise.

Our group has A$4.2m of cash across three entities, a A$1.5m overdraft at one entity, and a loan covenant requiring minimum group liquidity of A$2m. One subsidiary has local tax restrictions and another has a minority investor. Prepare a treasury decision memo with a cash-and-debt map, feasible internal funding alternatives, covenant implications, key legal/tax/bank restrictions, and recommended approval controls. Do not assume all subsidiary cash can be moved freely.

Create an authorised tabletop guide for security analysts explaining how an attacker may progress from reconnaissance through initial access, privilege escalation, defence evasion, and lateral movement in a mixed Windows and Linux estate. For each phase, give the objective, safe evidence sources analysts should inspect, likely detection gaps, and defensive improvements. Include a short reporting template that connects the narrative to business impact. Keep the material non-destructive, within scope, and limited to proof-of-concept validation.

A team is adding a partner integration that processes customer account data. Create an engineering responsibility plan that classifies the data, records trust boundaries and privacy implications, assigns access and review responsibilities, evaluates the supplier and credentials, and lists the evidence required before release. Cover implementation, review, build, test, release, and operation. Include a concise change-request checklist that links each decision to auditable evidence, while flagging any item requiring human approval.

Prepare a handoff report for an iOS change that adds a filter screen. The report must state the selected project context and simulator, build outcome, whether the app launched with captured diagnostics, and the completed outcome for each tested surface: opening the filter, applying a filter, clearing it, and returning to the list. Treat a failed observed check as failed until a later completed retest, and distinguish unperformed checks from passing ones. Stop subsequent UI claims if launch-with-diagnostics was not achieved.

A holding company has two trading subsidiaries, a central finance team, and shared IT costs. Management wants product profitability by division, while directors need legal-entity reporting for the close. Using the supplied headcount, revenue, transaction volume, and intercompany balances, propose the reporting views, defensible allocation drivers, treatment of controllable versus central costs, and governance checks for local authority and intercompany charges. Show pre- and post-allocation margins and flag items needing tax review.

Write a declarative mobile UI test for a desktop-style context action: focus a list row with a keyboard, open its context menu with a secondary pointer action, select “Rename”, type a new label, and assert the updated row after the UI becomes idle. Use stable node identification and node-relative interaction where appropriate. Include a verification checklist that the test avoids replacing this interaction with a touch-only gesture and that state assertions wait for recomposition.

Create a four-issue operating plan for a small professional community publication that alternates curated links, an interview, a teaching piece, and a trend summary. For each issue, define the opening, main feature, supporting material, community element, and closing action. Include a source-selection checklist, a sending schedule, subject-line principles, a lightweight promotion plan, and the metrics the editor should review after each send.

A distributor has A$620k in bank cash, payroll of A$280k due next week, overdue receivables of A$510k, slow inventory, and suppliers due A$340k within 14 days. Build a 13-week direct cash forecast with a downside case, diagnose receivable, payable, and inventory pressure, and prioritize immediate actions. Include trade-offs such as supply disruption and collection probability, plus a weekly control rhythm and named ownership for cash decisions.

Write a small program that uses authenticated library access to locate all records tagged “pilot-study”, create a new collection for the project, copy the matching records into it, and update one record's title after user confirmation. Export the resulting collection in both a machine-readable citation format and a bibliography format. Include pagination for a library larger than one page, handle write errors without silently retrying destructive changes, and print a concise summary of created, updated, and skipped items.

Perform an actionable dependency-health check on the supplied project. First determine the project's package ecosystem from its own files; if the required audit capability is unavailable, stop and report that limitation rather than guessing. Otherwise identify known vulnerabilities and outdated dependencies, rank them by urgency and likely impact, and provide a concise remediation queue with evidence. Do not perform a general code-quality review or make dependency changes.

Design the operating configuration for a distributed analysis service that runs 24 autonomous workers across three compute pools. Jobs have uneven durations, some workers will fail, and operators need to protect urgent jobs from long background runs. Deliver a topology and role layout, capacity and queue policy, load-balancing approach, retry and recovery rules, failure isolation strategy, and a monitoring dashboard specification with actionable alerts. This is a runtime-operation design, not a plan for merely dividing one assignment among people.

Prepare a dependency upgrade plan for an application scheduled for a maintenance release. Starting from its declared packages and resolved versions, classify available updates by compatibility risk, security relevance, and likely affected code. Produce a staged change plan, migration notes for risky updates, rollback points, and a test strategy for each stage. Do not recommend upgrading everything at once, and do not reduce the task to a security-only scan.

For a collaborative desktop planning app, propose a client-side data model that remains usable with 50,000 locally stored items and later converges changes from a user's laptop and tablet. Specify validated table shapes, fine-grained subscriptions that avoid redrawing unrelated views, durable local persistence, conflict semantics for concurrent edits, and a test matrix for restart and multi-device convergence. The output should be an architecture note and acceptance criteria, not a conventional server-only store or remote-query cache.

Audit the dependencies of a browser-based application before release. Identify known security issues, packages that are stale, declared packages with no demonstrated use, and dependencies that materially increase delivered client code. Compare declarations with the resolved dependency record, rank findings by risk and effort, and recommend changes with compatibility checks. Return an audit report only; do not automatically apply potentially breaking updates or turn this into a language-neutral upgrade plan.

Design the data layer for a field-sales web application whose account, visit, and note records originate in a central relational service. Representatives need fast local reads for only their assigned accounts, can create or edit notes without connectivity, and expect queued changes to replay safely when they reconnect. Deliver a sync-scope design, local data model, subscription rules, offline-write handling, conflict policy, and test cases for reassignment and reconnects. Exclude a server-rendered-only solution.

Coordinate a four-week accessibility improvement programme for a public-service website. The work must progress through intake, scope definition, evidence gathering, specialist assignments, independent reviews, synthesis, challenge review, and final handover. Produce a phase plan showing entry and exit criteria, responsibilities, dependencies, expected artefacts, and how conflicting findings will be reconciled. Do not perform the accessibility fixes themselves or treat this as a single-worker task.

We need to classify 480 independently collected survey responses by Friday. Create an execution plan that first identifies which checks can run independently, partitions the responses into balanced batches, limits concurrency to six workers, and merges the completed outputs into one verified result. Include a dependency check, batch-assignment table, aggregation and quality-control steps, and a fallback for a failed batch. Do not parallelise any validation that depends on a prior batch's conclusion.

A field-service app needs to remain useful during unreliable connectivity. Propose how staff should make changes to shared job records while disconnected and how those changes should be brought back into line with the shared system after a connection returns. Include what information a pending change should retain, how to handle competing edits from different devices, how to ensure an old update cannot bring back a record that was removed, and which kinds of action should require a live connection. Present the design as an implementation-ready outline for the product team.
